_help: Special encounters that need a short "how it works" explanation. Read by js/where.js. Each entry: id, title (bold heading), g = games it applies to, match = how to recognise the encounter in data/locations.json: method (the encounter method, e.g. "special") and cond (a regular expression tested, case-insensitive, against the row's condition text), intro = the explanation paragraphs. The explanation is shown once per Pokémon, as its own row under the first location row that has a matching encounter. Your normal location rows are unchanged.

encounters.title: N's Pokémon (special encounter)
intro: You need two DS / 3DS consoles: one with Pokémon Black or White where you have already beaten N and Ghetsis, and one with this game (Black 2 or White 2).

Connect them with Unova Link > Memory Link, then talk to the Breeder in the Aspertia City Pokémon Center and watch the cutscene where N releases his Pokémon. After that, each one has about a 1% chance to replace a normal wild encounter in its usual spot, and it stays there until you catch it.

encounters.title: Shadow Pokémon (snag and purify)
intro: Shadow Pokémon belong to a Cipher or Snagem trainer. Win the battle, then use the Snag Machine to snag the Shadow Pokémon instead of fighting it normally.

A Shadow Pokémon can't be traded or sent to another game until you purify it (Colosseum: Relic Stone / XD: Purification Chamber). Once purified, it can be sent to Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed and LeafGreen with a link cable.
Pokémon XD can only trade with the Game Boy Advance games on the original GameCube release. The Nintendo Classics (Switch 2) version cannot link to them.

encounters.title: Shiny locked (XD)
intro: In Pokémon XD, almost every Shadow Pokémon is shiny locked, so it can never be shiny. Only 17 Pokémon can be shiny: Eevee, Chikorita, Cyndaquil, Totodile, Larvitar, Meditite, Shuckle, Elekid and the PokéSpot Pokémon (Zubat, Aron, Wooper, Sandshrew, Gligar, Trapinch, Hoppip, Phanpy, Surskit). Rows marked "shiny locked" below can't be shiny.

encounters.title: Miror B.'s 2nd Chances (missed Shadow Pokémon)
intro: Some Shadow Pokémon belong to trainers who don't stay in one place (Cipher Admins and wandering Cipher Peons). If you miss one, Miror B. steals it, and you get a second chance to snag it from him.

Once you have found Miror B., a radar alert tells you where he is. He can turn up anywhere: at a PokéSpot, in a town or at a stadium. He will battle you with the stolen Pokémon as many times as it takes for you to snag it.
When every one of the 83 Shadow Pokémon is snagged, whether from him or from their trainers, he destroys the radar. The levels listed here are the ones he uses.

Snag rule: a Shadow Pokémon you snag does not appear in your party or PC until you win the battle. If you lose after snagging it, it either goes back to its trainer or runs off and joins Miror B.'s team, exactly as if you had won without snagging it.

encounters.title: In-game trades (XD)
intro: Two NPCs trade you a Pokémon for one of yours. Hordel (Outskirt Stand) wants a purified Shadow Togepi or Togetic and gives a Lv 20 Elekid. Duking swaps rare PokéSpot Pokémon: Surskit for Shuckle, Trapinch for Meditite, Wooper for Larvitar (all Lv 20).
These trades give you Pokémon you cannot get any other way in this game, so keep the PokéSpot rarities.

encounters.title: Johto starters (Mt. Battle)
intro: Beat 100 opponents in a row in Mt. Battle with the same party and you can pick one Johto starter (Lv 5). Redo the challenge to get the others.
Each one knows its own signature move: Chikorita has Frenzy Plant, Cyndaquil has Blast Burn and Totodile has Hydro Cannon.

encounters.title: Japan only (Bonus Disc)
intro: This Pokémon came from the Japanese Colosseum Bonus Disc. It was never available in the North American or PAL versions of the game.

encounters.title: North America only (Bonus Disc)
intro: This Pokémon (Jirachi) came from the North American Colosseum Bonus Disc. It was never available in the Japanese or PAL versions of the game.

encounters.title: Japan only (e-Reader card)
intro: These Shadow Pokémon (Togepi, Mareep, Scizor) came from Japanese e-Reader cards scanned in the Card e Room. The cards were only released in Japan, so you can't get them in the North American or PAL versions.
